floor_history.headline: Recon s1: floor re-measured 32 (chassis unchanged, all WIP-imported verdicts spendable); $v0/$v1 exchange confirmed at .greg disposition level (pseudo 100 in $v1, 83/84/98 in $v0); frontier = instrume

Structural respelling dropped the honest floor 32 -> 14 and RETRACTS the s1 'RA exchange validated unreachable' verdict: every $v0/$v1 hunk inverse.py had foreclosed closed under ordinary shared-named

Structural session: honest floor 14 -> 2 and build_insns now 231 == target 231; duplicating the tail addend and the >>12 into both use_high arms (sanctioned duplicated-statement-into-arms, merged back

Permuter measured dead on the floor-2 residual (3 chassis, ~45 min, ~35k iters, zero sub-60 finds) and control-flow exit forms proven inert; in exchange the divergence is now pinned exactly to sched2'

Forensics RETRACTS s4's LUID-lock verdict: the LUID tie-break already yields target's order and is overridden by schedule_select's potential-hazard rule (sched.c:2707-2723); the chain's pri-47 is a $v

frontier.hypothesis: Lifting the synth-mult chain into priority group 48 (from 47) removes it from schedule_select's comparison with the pri-47 gp store entirely, and produces target's emitted order.
frontier.mechanism: The only thing pinning the chain at 47 is the $v1 WAR anti-dependence on insn 93. If the chain's first insn anti/output-depends on a pri->=48 insn instead (the mult 105, or the mflos 111/531/534), the whole chain inherits >= 48; schedule_select processes priority groups in descending order, so the chain is picked first and the store is emitted ahead of it. This is a register-allocation property - the same axis that took the floor 14 -> 2 in s3 - not a value property.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the s3 lever family (which local carries the 0x9C4/0x2710 value, declaration order, variable reuse, where its consumer sits) but grade each variant by the DIRECT observable rather than the score: run tmp/grind/func_8001B748/s5/dump.sh on it and read PRIODBG SET insn=<chain tail> final_pri (win = >= 48 while the gp store stays 47). tools/ra_solver (inverse.py global, pseudo_scope.py) can test reachability of the register goal 'the early-exit synth chain lands in any hard register whose previous reader/writer has pri >= 48'.

frontier.hypothesis: Equalising potential_hazard between the chain tail and the gp store flips the pick without touching priorities at all.
frontier.mechanism: schedule_select scans the priority group with a STRICTLY-greater test (if ((cost = potential_hazard(...)) > best_cost)) over ready[], which rank_for_schedule sorted DESCENDING by LUID within the group - so the chain tail (luid 38) is scanned BEFORE the gp store (luid 25) and wins any tie. It therefore needs only an EQUAL hazard, which any unit-0 memory-class insn (codes 125/159/163) has, versus 0 for a unit-less ALU insn (codes 3/16/181).
frontier.next_probe: Shape the 0x9C4/0x2710 sequence so its LAST insn before the store comparison is memory-class (e.g. the >> 12 and the store fused so the final insn is the sh/sw or a move) rather than an sll/addu. Confirm by the ABSENCE of a SELBEST line at that clock in full.log - a SELBEST ... pos>0 line is exactly the override - then score with tmp/grind/func_8001B748/s4/score.py (~2 s per variant).

frontier.hypothesis: Lowering the gp store below priority 47 is the weakest of the three axes because the a8/b8 loads pin it.
frontier.mechanism: final_pri(116)=47 has three contributors all at 47: an OUTPUT-dep on the dst+4 store (98) and ANTI-deps on the a+8 / b+8 loads (103/109). Reassociating the multiply pairs can move the store term, but the loads stay at 47 and re-pin it.
frontier.next_probe: Only if F-A and F-B both come back dead: probe the single form that could work - make the gp store's ENTIRE memory-dependence set live upstream of the 4th mflo (528), i.e. have the a8/b8 loads issue before the a4/a6 multiplies - and read PRIODBG SET insn=<gp store> final_pri to check for 46 or lower.
